app.description: Android app under backdoor detection analysis by EchoDroid

backdoor_verdict.verdict_explanation: Moderate mismatch signals; warrants further manual investigation.

backdoor_patterns.explanation: The app declares android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE in the manifest, but backend analysis shows no evidence of this permission being exercised at runtime and the UI never mentions phone state or device ID access. This may indicate a zombie permission for future activation or to evade static analysis.

android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared in the manifest, but there is no evidence of storage access in backend analysis and no mention in the UI. This could be a placeholder for future use or an attempt to mask true intent.

Two non-UI exported components (com.sBKMD.ujQQLoKHkeFa and com.sBKMD.userPermissionReceiver) are accessible externally, but their functionality is not described in the UI or backend analysis. Exported components with obfuscated names are a common backdoor pattern, as they may be triggered by other apps or remote commands to execute hidden logic.
